A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Implicit-ARAP. Their complete text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v3's supplementary Sections 6–8. Substantial reorganization does not prevent matching the research content.

before.justification: V2 reports original deformation experiments on TFD and DeFAUST, baseline comparisons, and patch-meshing and sensitivity analyses in Section 5.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds DT4D comparisons, SDF-preservation measurements and further analyses in Sections 4 and 7.

M1.justification: Local patch construction, roto-translation deformation fields, handle and ARAP losses, and the invertible and ordinary MLP architectures are retained. The new pseudocode documents the existing procedure rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: V3 adds animation-derived deformation pairs from DeformingThings4D in Sections 7.3–7.4. TFD and DeFAUST remain, making this an extension of data coverage within the existing mesh-deformation task.

E2.justification: V3 adds Neural Shape Deformation Priors (NSDP) as an evaluated comparator on DT4D in Table 5. Figure 4 also adds NFGP to the existing ablation comparison. ARAP, Elastic, SR-ARAP and NFGP remain in the corresponding main benchmark tables.

E3.justification: V3 adds target-shape evaluation, gradient-norm measurements over one million spatial samples, loss-weight sweeps and comparisons with matched patch/mesh edge lengths. It also reports a changed default ARAP-loss weight for TFD neural-field experiments: 10 in v2 Table 1 versus 1000 in v3 Table 2. This does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands analysis through quantitative SDF-preservation checks, sphere-traced renders, target-shape agreement, loss balancing and matched-resolution experiments. It adds qualitative patch-parameter sweeps while retaining earlier sensitivity plots. Conversely, v2's dinosaur comparisons and one-versus-ten-handle case study are absent.

E5.justification: V3 Figure 4 and Table 8 introduce standard-deviation reporting for sampled SDF gradient norms; v2's corresponding ablation was qualitative. These statistics describe spatial variability, not uncertainty across repeated runs. Neither version reports experimental seeds or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results on DT4D, target matching, SDF preservation and sensitivity. Table 5 reports volume errors of 0.58% versus 7.80% for Implicit-ARAP and NSDP, but runtimes of 6m:33s versus 18s. Most original benchmark entries remain; NFGP's DeFAUST neural-field EL changes from 9.63% in v2 Table 4 to 8.71% in v3 Table 1.

T1.justification: V3 Section 4.1 corrects the inverse-mapping relation in v2 Section 3.2: the source point satisfies x = d_phi(x'), rather than x' = d_phi(x). The defining inverse-composition equation was already correct. Other mathematical formulations are retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain local patch meshing, ARAP-based neural deformation and efficient handle-guided editing of neural fields and high-resolution meshes. V3 foregrounds neural fields in its title and abstract, but retains the mesh contribution in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands discussion of SDF-preservation limitations, handle-fit versus rigidity tradeoffs, and the distinction between target-shape agreement and deformation correctness. Section 4.2 also changes the proposed explanation for marching-cubes failures: fixed discretizations may permit misleading local optima, whereas v2 emphasized missing regularization away from the zero level set.

D1.justification: V3 adds sampling/training pseudocode, patch counts of n=2000 and m=1000, rendering implementation information and asset licenses. However, it drops CPU/RAM specifications, detailed DeFAUST construction information and explicit benchmark-exclusion disclosures. Most architecture and optimizer details are relocated; both code links remain placeholders.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive discussion of Neural Jacobian Fields, NSDP, spatial and cage-based deformation, and feature-based neural editing. New differential-operator references support using discrete ARAP objectives. These additions broaden the context while retaining the central positioning relative to NFGP and classical ARAP methods.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract and substantial explanatory passages, foregrounds neural-field experiments, and moves mesh evaluation and implementation material into supplementary sections. It introduces a contents page, explicit limitations and a reorganized document hierarchy.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to one, transposes benchmark tables, merges projection illustrations, splits sensitivity panels and adds several analytical displays. Existing figures are extensively relocated and rearranged. V3 Figure 13 also clips much of the cube-deformation row that was fully visible in v2 Figure 10.

improvement.justification: The added SDF-preservation checks, NSDP and target-shape comparisons, and failure analyses make the validation and applicability boundaries more informative. Pseudocode and sampling counts improve reproducibility. These benefits are partly offset by lost benchmark-exclusion and preprocessing details and the clipped cube comparison in Figure 13, supporting a limited net improvement.
